about: Short chess questions a child or parent may ask (rules and history). Reference answers for grading; `mustMention` is checked automatically, the rest by reading.

items.question: What is en passant?
items.reference: A pawn that moves two squares from its starting square and lands beside an enemy pawn can be captured by that pawn as if it had moved one square; only on the very next move.

items.question: Who was India's first grandmaster, and in which year?
Can a pawn promote to a king?
items.reference: No. A pawn promotes to a queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour, never a king (or a pawn).

items.question: If a player has no legal move but is not in check, who wins?
items.reference: Nobody: it is stalemate and the game is a draw.

items.question: My king moved one square and then went back to its first square. Can I still castle?
items.reference: No. Once the king has moved, castling is no longer allowed for the rest of the game, even if it returns.
